question.text: A stock trades at Rs. 750. A put option with strike Rs. 800 has a premium of Rs. 75. What is the intrinsic value and time value?

answer.text: Intrinsic value: Rs. 50, Time value: Rs. 25
Intrinsic value: Rs. 75, Time value: Rs. 0
Intrinsic value: Rs. 0, Time value: Rs. 75
Intrinsic value: Rs. 25, Time value: Rs. 50

explanation.text: The Logic: Put Intrinsic Value = max(X - S, 0) = max(800 - 750, 0) = Rs. 50. Time Value = Premium - Intrinsic Value = 75 - 50 = Rs. 25. The put is ITM because S < X, so the premium splits into both intrinsic and time value components. The Trap: "IV Rs. 75, TV Rs. 0" treats the whole premium as intrinsic value, which would only be true for a deep-ITM expiring option. "IV Rs. 0, TV Rs. 75" treats the option as OTM. "IV Rs. 25, TV Rs. 50" inverts the two figures. Note: Broken comparison after "This put is ITM (S" repaired — explanation now states "the put is ITM because S < X."
